answer: Weight agents by measured capacity, not key count, as Tor does. Tor's bandwidth scanners push test traffic through every relay and weight it by the throughput they observe, so splitting one server into ten relays only splits the same share. A ledger could send each key surprise timed inference jobs, run concurrently: fifty keys on one GPU kernel share one throughput budget and each crawls at glacier pace. Spread across that tundra of slow keys, the farm's total reward stays flat, so extra identities earn nothing.
